boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Marietta [Operations] record (June 9-July 3, 1864; aggregate operation) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. The frozen row is an aggregate operation listing Brushy Mountain, Gilgal Church, Lost Mountain, Mud Creek, Noonday Creek, Pine Mountain and other actions. Kolb's Farm (GA014, June 22) and Kennesaw Mountain (GA015, June 27) are separate frozen records inside this interval; their strengths and losses are not repeated or added here. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the two armies without counts; the live field reads zero. Cox says Blair's corps arrived on June 8 with about nine thousand men, almost exactly equal to Sherman's losses to that time, and that Georgia militia, a full division at least, were known to be in the field. His Appendix A lists 3,800 Georgia militia at Kenesaw on June 20 and 86,475 Confederates before the Chattahoochee crossing, and Johnston's July 10 return (aggregate present and absent 135,092, present 73,849, effectives 50,932). Johnston gives Smith's militia division an effective total of about 1,500 on July 1 and the force transferred to Hood as about 41,000 infantry and artillery and 10,000 cavalry.
claims.rationale: Reinforcement, reconstructed and return figures on different dates and bases; the militia figures conflict (3,800 against about 1,500). None is a count for the operation and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Johnston says the army fell back on the night of July 2 because the Federal right was nearer Atlanta than the Confederate left; Cox says Johnston evacuated Kenesaw and the whole front that night. NPS says Sherman forced Johnston out of the Marietta area on July 2-3.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown; the live field reads 0 (US 0; CS 0). Cox gives monthly figures only: Union killed, wounded and missing of 7,500 in June; Johnston's hospital returns of 4,000 killed and wounded for the month; and his own reconstruction of Confederate losses at 7,000 or more. Johnston gives about 10,000 killed and wounded and 4,700 other losses of infantry and artillery from May 5 to July 17.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. These are monthly or campaign totals that include Kolb's Farm, Kennesaw and days outside the frozen interval; they are context and must not be assigned to this record or added to GA014/GA015. The live zeros are not measured absence.

open_questions: The component actions' reports (Pine Mountain, Gilgal Church, Mud Creek, Noonday Creek and others), Sherman's and the army commanders' reports, Hardee's itinerary and the compiled returns remain deferred. The associated battles listed in the frozen row are not individually researched.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Johnston's October 20, 1864 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, is a third family (interested Confederate account). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
